articles.title_orig: Israel Election Live Updates: Record Voter Turnout as Netanyahu Faces Challenge Led by Eisenkot
articles.title_zh: Israel Election Live Updates: Record Voter Turnout as Netanyahu Faces Challenge Led by Eisenkot
articles.content_orig:
Jerusalem 10:15 p.m. Oct. 27
Aaron Boxerman David M. Halbfinger Leo Sands and Max Bearak
Polls have closed in an election that has seen Israelis vote in record numbers. In what is widely seen as the most consequential election in the country’s history, voters were deciding whether to keep Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his far-right coalition in power or chart a new course.
By 8 p.m. local time (2 p.m. Eastern), two hours before polls were scheduled to close, 74.3 percent of eligible voters had cast ballots, the highest rate for that point in the day since 1988.
Turnout appeared to be particularly high among Arab citizens, who make up about a fifth of Israel’s population. By late afternoon, hours before the polls were set to close, turnout in some Arab-majority towns had exceeded the totals from the last election, in 2022.
Responding to the high turnout in those towns, Mr. Netanyahu accused Arab citizens of “trying to steal the elections,” repeatedly using brazen and overtly racial appeals to push his right-wing base to vote. An attempt by his Likud party on Tuesday to have voting hours extended was rejected by the Central Election Committee.
The election is Israel’s first since the Hamas-led attacks on Oct. 7, 2023, which was the deadliest day for Jews since the Holocaust and ignited three years of war that left Gaza largely in ruins and nearly all its population displaced.
Voters have a choice between two blocs offering starkly different visions. Mr. Netanyahu, the leader of the most far-right government in Israeli history, built a coalition of nationalists and ultra-Orthodox Jews, which faces an ideologically diverse group of Jewish opposition parties loosely led by Gadi Eisenkot , a former military chief of staff whose son was killed in the Gaza war. Parties representing Arab citizens of Israel also staunchly oppose Mr. Netanyahu’s government.
Both sides are framing the election as a make-or-break moment for the country. Mr. Netanyahu’s coalition offers the promise of a more religious Israel with an ever-tighter grip over the West Bank and Gaza. His opponents are casting the vote as the last chance to preserve democracy and pull Israel back from the brink of becoming a pariah state under international sanctions.
Voting will close at 10 p.m. (4 p.m. Eastern time), but there is unlikely to be an immediate determination of who will be the next prime minister. Opinion polls suggest that Mr. Netanyahu’s allies and rivals are roughly tied, and assembling a governing coalition in Israel’s parliamentary system could take weeks or months .
Opposition leaders led by Mr. Eisenkot have called for a reckoning over what they call Mr. Netanyahu’s failure to prevent the catastrophic Oct. 7 attacks. They also have pledged to repair Israel’s shattered image abroad , including by cracking down on Israeli extremist violence against Palestinians in the occupied West Bank.
Mr. Netanyahu has resisted the establishment of an independent commission to investigate the Oct. 7 attacks. He has vowed to move ahead with overhauling Israel’s judicial system, a move that critics say could undermine the country’s liberal democracy. And his allies say they hope to permanently entrench Israeli rule in the West Bank and Gaza despite international condemnation.
The 77-year-old leader has dominated Israeli politics for decades. In recent days, he repeatedly suggested that the country could face annihilation without him in charge.
Here’s what else to watch:
Key issues: In a tumultuous campaign, several issues divided Israeli voters. Read more ›
West Bank and Gaza: As Israelis headed to the polls, Palestinians in the West Bank were under an Israeli military lockdown. Palestinians in the West Bank and Gaza cannot vote in Israeli elections, but they may have much to lose if Mr. Netanyahu’s coalition stays in power. Read more ›
Netanyahu sows doubt: Mr. Netanyahu used racially charged language to cast suspicion over high turnout among Arab citizens and to encourage his base to go to the polls. Election officials said Tuesday that there had been no indication of widespread irregularities.
Trump weighs in: President Trump has endorsed Mr. Netanyahu , praising him as an important partner in the war against Iran and saying anyone else would be the “wrong leader” for Israel. Analysts were skeptical that the U.S. president’s intervention would sway many voters.
Initial exit polls showed that no clear victor was yet in sight as the voting drew to a close Tuesday night. The polls indicated that, against the odds, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s Likud party held a small lead over the party of Gadi Eisenkot, a former military chief, in Israel’s pivotal parliamentary election. But the anti-Netanyahu bloc, including two predominantly Arab parties, held a wide lead over the prime minister and his allies in exit polls published by Israel’s main television networks.
The polls have now closed in Israel. People who are in line to vote will still be able to do so.
No party is expected to achieve a clear victory, which means the election will likely only be the first step in determining who will form the next government. Here’s how that might unfold.
The first projections of results in Israel’s election are about to be made public when the country’s major television networks publish their exit polls at 10 p.m. local time, when voting precincts close except to those already in line. Caveats abound: The exit polls have a spotty history of accuracy but give an initial sense of the relative strength of the parties. The closer fought the election, the riskier it is to place much stock in them. And this is just the beginning of what can be a drawn-out process to determine who will form Israel’s next government.
Polls have closed in Israel, and initial exit polls by Israeli broadcasters are expected to be released shortly afterward. But it will be hours before the definitive results are known, and it could be weeks until a new government is formed.
Early indicator: Exit polls in Israel can be useful to get a sense of each party’s relative strength, but they are not considered a reliable gauge of precise results — particularly in a tight race like this one.
Vote-counting: Votes are tallied in Israel by hand, with ballot slips tabulated at more than 12,000 polling places across the country. The counters are monitored by camera-toting election observers.
First results: After the hand count is completed, paper tallies are taken to regional hubs where the results are recorded electronically. The whole process takes hours, and the authorities begin to release the results once they are completed.
Possible delay: Israel is a parliamentary democracy, and no party is expected to win anywhere near an outright majority of the votes. Once the results are in, the process of forming a government will begin. That could take weeks or even months.
Next government: The party with the most votes and the most seats in the Parliament may not be the one to form a government. In 2021, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s Likud party won the most seats but was unable to assemble a majority coalition. Instead, after months of wrangling, an eclectic coalition of anti-Netanyahu forces cobbled together a single-seat majority in Parliament.
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s governing coalition has the distinction of surviving for a full four-year term in office, something no government in Israel has achieved for more than 30 years. Since first taking office in 1996, he has tallied 19 years in power and become Israel’s longest-serving prime minister by far.
On Tuesday, he is seeking a seventh term, in Israel’s first parliamentary election since the deadly Hamas-led attack in 2023 that prompted its devastating war in Gaza.
The longevity of his most recent governing coalition followed three years during which a cycle of collapsed coalitions and five snap elections had left the country without a functional government or national budge

articles.title_orig: Donald Trump Jr. Hunted In Mongolia With Russian Oligarch Umar Kremlev Who Bankrolled His Wedding, Report Says
articles.title_zh: Donald Trump Jr. Hunted In Mongolia With Russian Oligarch Umar Kremlev Who Bankrolled His Wedding, Report Says
articles.content_orig:
President Donald Trump apepars at a rally at Alico Arena on the Florida Gulf Coast University campus on Oct. 23, 2026, in Fort Myers, Florida.
A woman who had accused President Donald Trump of sexually assaulting her in 1993 described it to congressional staff as rape and said the interaction left her bleeding and bruised, according to a report released Monday by Democrats on the House Judiciary Committee examining Trump's ties to Jeffrey Epstein.
Beatrice Keul, a model and former Miss Switzerland, alleged to Judiciary Committee staff that she was raped by Trump in a Plaza Hotel suite in Manhattan when she was 24. Keul said that while attending the American Dream Pageant, which had a partnership with Trump, she met with Trump at a press luncheon at the event.
Trump, according to Keul, promised to arrange her visa in the U.S. and ensure her acceptance into New York University through his friend Paolo Zampolli, a close Trump ally who was, until earlier this month, part of his Administration. At the same event, she also spent at least 10 minutes talking to Epstein who she said claimed to have organized “many parties with Don.”
Later that day, Keul alleges, Trump invited her to a hotel suite where Trump “grabbed Keul from behind and forcibly raped her,” causing “bleeding and bruising on multiple parts of her body,” the report says. Following the incident, Keul alleges Trump made her promise she would keep quiet and repeated his promise for visa and college admission.
Because Keul’s passport had been taken from her on her arrival, she was not able to leave the contest following the incident, she alleges, according to the report. After she returned to Switzerland, she declined to participate in an additional Trump-sponsored pageant in Hawaii several weeks later.
TIME has been unable to independently verify details of Keul’s account.
In a statement, the White House denies the allegations and says that President Trump has been “fully exonerated of anything related to Epstein.” “This ‘report’ is nothing more than a desperate attempt by crazed Democrats to distract Americans from the surging Republican momentum driven by President Trump’s historic achievements,” White House spokeswoman Lauren Bis says.
Keul has previously spoken in public about her sexual assault allegations against Trump, but the report provided new details of the alleged rape—as well as reviewing similar accounts of other Trump accusers.
Read more: Trump Said He Banned Epstein From Mar-a-Lago. A Lawmaker Who Reviewed Unredacted Files Says They Tell a Different Story
In addition to Keul’s account, the report also compiled allegations from four other women who have directly accused Trump of rape or sexual assault in connection with the Epstein investigation. The allegations, spanning from the mid-1980s to the 1990s, had all been previously made public either through media interviews or FBI testimony released as part of the Epstein files.
The report’s release, just over a week before Election Day, comes as Democrats are working to signal to voters how they will make use of their power if they gain control of one or both chambers of Congress.
On Monday, Rep. Jamie Raskin of Maryland, the top Democrat of the House Judiciary Committee, called on the Department of Justice to appoint an independent special counsel to oversee the investigation of allegations mentioned in the report. So far, Ghislaine Maxwell , a longtime Epstein confidant, is the only person to have been convicted of sex trafficking of minors in connection with the Epstein case.
“An independent special counsel must investigate Epstein’s co-conspirators and DOJ’s cover-up and ensure that state and foreign prosecutors have the evidence they need to pursue justice,” Raskin said in a statement.
The report also alleges that Zampolli, a former Trump administration official and a close Trump ally, was “an active participant” in the Epstein sex trafficking allegations.
According to the report, which cites multiple FBI reports included in the Epstein files, Zampolli arranged U.S. visas for young female models before they met Epstein. One FBI report mentioned that Zampolli arranged an 18-year-old model’s visa before she was recruited to give a massage at Epstein’s house, where Epstein allegedly raped her.
Zampolli himself has also been accused of rape and sexual assault in a separate case brought by model Victoria Drake, who alleges in an ongoing civil lawsuit that Zampolli drugged and raped her in 2023.
TIME has reached out to Zampolli for comment.
Previously, Zampolli has claimed that he had introduced First Lady Melania Trump to the President in 1998, but the report disputes that claim, citing two accounts—one from an unnamed Epstein associate and the other from Amanda Ungaro, a Brazilian model—saying that Epstein had introduced Melania Trump to Donald Trump.
The New York Times reported in March that Zampolli had asked a top official at Immigration and Customs Enforcement  last year to detain and deport Ungaro, whom Zampolli had previously dated, amid a custody battle over their son. Zampolli denied making such requests.
Until earlier this month, Zampolli held a diplomatic role under the State Department as Special Representative for Global Partnerships. He was fired two weeks ago over a months-long dispute with the department’s deputy secretary, according to Politico .

articles.title_orig: Mbappe seeks to defuse China anger after 'ill-judged' Mao comments
articles.title_zh: Mbappe seeks to defuse China anger after 'ill-judged' Mao comments
articles.content_orig:
A backlash has erupted on Chinese social media over MbappÃ©'s comments on a "Chinese dictator"
Kylian MbappÃ© has apologised for "ill-judged" comments he made about late Chinese leader Mao Zedong which led to him being dropped by several Chinese brands.
MbappÃ© had reportedly told French talk show The Bridge the meme "that makes me laugh the most, it's the one where there's a video of a guy, I think it's a Chinese dictator..." He then laughs as the clip cuts to a meme showing his face superimposed on an image resembling Mao.
The meme is part of a running joke about the Real Madrid forward being called a "dictator" because of his huge influence in football.
"My comment was ill-judged, and I now understand that it hurt many people in China and in Chinese communities around the world,"  MbappÃ© said in a statement.
"I apologise to everyone my words have upset."
Spain's La Liga also apologised, saying it "deeply regrets the offence that Kylian MbappÃ©'s recent comments have caused among Chinese fans".
The joke did not go down well in China, where Mao is revered by the Communist Party, despite his chaotic and often violent rule that left millions dead.
A few people came out in support of him on Chinese social media, but that is a rare response given China's tightly controlled internet, where people are expected to toe the party and government line on sensitive topics.
Few topics are as sensitive as Mao, which may explain why brands were so quick to terminate partnerships with a global sports star like MbappÃ©.
The original video is not available on the show's YouTube channel, and it's unclear when the interview hosted by Real Madrid's AurÃ©lien TchouamÃ©ni first aired. In clips that have been circulating online, MbappÃ© does not identify Mao by name. He says he "uses [the meme] with friends all the time".
The furore appeared to kick off on Monday night after Chinese football forum Dongqiudi drew attention to the comments in a statement, saying they were "inappropriate" and "hurt the feelings of Chinese people".
Screengrabs of the clip and meme have since spread quickly on Chinese social media, with people echoing this sentiment and even calling for a boycott of both the French striker and his club, Real Madrid.
But some have blurred the meme itself as well as the part of the comment they found offensive, when Mbappe refers to "a Chinese dictator".
Dongqiudi said in its statement that it was "unable to translate" his comments because they were "offensive to China and the Chinese people".
Many people are therefore also wondering what exactly Mbappe said and have responded to the angry posts and comments with questions, wanting to know more.
Weibo users are recirculating the clip by blurring the meme and redacting references to Mao
Chinese fans have been criticising MbappÃ© â who is popular in China and has huge brand endorsements â of "profiting from the Chinese market yet making remarks that offend the Chinese public".
"International public figures, in particular, should show greater respect and sensitivity, as national sentiment must never be taken lightly," reads another  comment on Weibo.
As the anger online grew louder, Chinese brands began to cut ties, although they did not explicitly refer to the video.
The country's largest dairy producer, Mengniu, said it "firmly opposes and has a zero-tolerance policy towards any words or actions that hurt the feelings of the Chinese people".
Drinks giant Dongpeng issued a similar statement: "Our company firmly opposes and has a zero-tolerance policy towards any behaviour that offends national sentiments."
According to state-owned newspaper The Global Times, state broadcaster CCTV's news apps will not feature content related to the French striker. CCTV will also stop showing La Liga matches, Chinese media reported on Tuesday. Real Madrid is one of 20 clubs that play in the Spanish football league and is the most decorated team with 36 league titles.
China's foreign ministry has also weighed in, with spokesperson Lin Jian saying: "We have noted the relevant reports. Words and deeds that hurt the feelings of the Chinese people will naturally be met with opposition from all sectors of Chinese society."
MbappÃ© has a significant commercial presence in China
China is a major market for international sports stars and homegrown brands have signed multimillion-dollar endorsement contracts with MbappÃ©, Norwegian striker Erling Haaland, and NBA player Stephen Curry.
By 14:00 local time on Tuesday, five of the top 10 trending topics on Weibo centered on MbappÃ©, with the hashtag "multiple brands terminate partnerships with MbappÃ©" topping the list.
"Don't ever come to China," read one of the top comments on Weibo.
Mao founded the People's Republic of China in 1949 and ruled through tumultuous decades in the 1960s and 1970s.
His attempt at rapid industrialisation, which he called the Great Leap Forward, led to a famine that killed tens of millions. Then came the Cultural Revolution: a violent purge of anyone seen as a threat to Communism, which included Chinese intellectuals, landowners, artists and often rivals within the Party.
His death in 1976 brought a new era for China, which began to open its doors to the global economy. Even as the country moved away from Mao's rule, he continued to be hailed by the party as a national icon whose legacy was beyond reproach.
So jokes or memes about Mao are seen not just as an insult to the party but also its closely-guarded narrative about the country's past.
MbappÃ© has said some of the memes "reveal a lack of political and human awareness"
It's unclear when the MbappÃ© meme involving Mao began but his nickname, "the dictator", has made the striker the subject of many memes and jokes online.
MbappÃ© is widely regarded as one of the best footballers in the world and has wielded significant influence at the clubs he has played for. His extraordinary speed, goalscoring ability and worldwide popularity have made him a global icon, attracting millions of fans, major sponsorship deals and media attention, with his influence extending into fashion, culture and business.
In 2024, he sued a French influencer and kebab shop owner for using his name in the description of one of the shop's sandwiches, leading to more jokes about the nickname.
France teammate Ousmane Dembele jumped on the trend during the 2026 World Cup, calling MbappÃ© Mobut â a reference to Mobutu Sese Seko, the dictator who ruled the Democratic Republic of Congo, formerly Zaire, for three decades.
In an interview with France Football in September, MbappÃ© acknowledged the light-heartedness behind many of these memes, but said they "sometimes reveal a lack of political and human awareness among people".
"There's a side that's a bit less funny, because we know the damage people like that have caused throughout history," he said.
"Being compared to people who murder others, or who have made millions upon millions of people miserable... I don't think I've done that in my life."
Additional reporting by Fan Wang and Osmond Chia

articles.title_orig: Live Updates: 8-month Iran war looms over Israeli election as Egypt wades into Saudi's fight with the Houthis
articles.title_zh: Live Updates: 8-month Iran war looms over Israeli election as Egypt wades into Saudi's fight with the Houthis
articles.content_orig:
International Atomic Energy Agency chief Rafael Grossi urged Iran during a U.N. Security Council meeting on Tuesday to grant immediate access to his agency so it can verify the Islamic republic's nuclear materials.
The IAEA has not had access to key nuclear facilities in Iran since Israel and the United States launched strikes on nuclear sites in June 2025.
Nuclear facilities have also been hit in the latest war, and the IAEA has repeatedly called for access.
"I invite Iran to work with the IAEA without any further delay to clarify outstanding safeguards questions and to give the IAEA the information and access the agency requires, so that it can verify all relevant facilities and material, as is Iran's legal obligation," Grossi said.
The Security Council meeting followed a resolution passed by the IAEA board last month that referred Iran to the top U.N. body over its nuclear "non-compliance."
The resolution, submitted by Britain, France, Germany and the United States, marks the first time Iran has been referred to the Security Council in 20 years for failing to comply with its nuclear reporting obligations.
The move has been seen as largely symbolic as China and Russia hold power to veto any sanctions against their ally Tehran. Both countries were joined by Niger in voting against the IAEA resolution.
Nearly 100 fighters have been killed in renewed clashes between Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis and Saudi-backed government forces in southwestern Yemen, military sources from both sides told the AFP news agency on Tuesday.
At least 63 Houthi fighters and 34 pro-government combatants have died, mostly near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, the Red Sea's strategic southern chokepoint, they said.
The clashes, which began with airstrikes late on Monday, are the fiercest since the Houthis seized swathes of territory from the Saudi-backed government in a lightning offensive last month.
The Houthis fought off "an attempted advance by Saudi enemy forces ... from the southern direction of Bab al-Mandab," military spokesman Yahya Saree posted on X, describing "a large number of dead and wounded."
The Houthi military sources said Saudi Arabia carried out dozens of airstrikes, hitting Mayyun Island in the strait as well as Dhubab and Mocha further up the Red Sea coast.
Government military sources said intense fighting was under way in the Bab el-Mandeb area, claiming they had made progress on the ground.
Earlier this month, Yemen's government launched a counteroffensive with Saudi air support to try to reclaim the territory lost to the Houthis.
But the campaign has faltered, while the Houthis have ramped up deadly attacks on Saudi Arabia that shuttered its capital's airport for two weeks and disrupted daily life.
Riyadh leads a military coalition that first intervened in the conflict in 2015. The fighting has devastated Yemen and created one of the world's worst humanitarian crises.
Russian President Vladimir Putin and his Iranian counterpart, President Masoud Pezeshkian, discussed working together on oil and gas projects as the two met in person at the Gas Exporting Countries Forum Summit in Moscow on Tuesday.
The two leaders "discussed expanding political, economic, trade and energy cooperation, including joint projects in the oil and gas sectors," according to a readout from the Iranian government .
Pezeshkian also discussed working together on natural gas exports. Iran ranks third in the world in natural gas production — 280 billion cubic meters per year, according to the president — behind only the U.S. and Russia.
"Pezeshkian emphasized that global developments necessitate joint technical-engineering cooperation and strategic governance across international energy markets," the government said, presumably referring to the war with the U.S.
Russia and Iran have worked together for years. As the war in Ukraine continues, Russia continues to purchase Shahed drones for use in attacks.
The two countries have rarely coordinated on energy projects, however, as both countries produce massive amounts of crude on their own. The timing of the discussion Tuesday in Russia is especially important though because Iran has been cut off from importing or exporting crude due to the U.S. blockade on Iranian ports.
France's deputy chief of mission in Tehran was this month subjected to "intimidation by individuals claiming to belong to the Iranian security forces," a diplomatic source told the AFP news agency on Tuesday.
The incident, the second involving French diplomats in Tehran in less than four months, highlights the sharp deterioration in relations between France and Iran.
In response to the mistreatment of the diplomat in early October, Iran's ambassador to France was summoned by the French foreign ministry, the source said, without specifying the exact date of the summons.
"He was reminded in the strongest terms that we expect the Iranian authorities to take all necessary measures to guarantee the security of our personnel and premises," the source said.
French magazine Le Point , which first reported the incident, said the diplomat was forcibly stopped in the street by members of Iran's security forces, in breach of his diplomatic status. The encounter culminated in what the magazine described as a forceful interrogation.
The episode follows a July incident involving two French diplomats based in Tehran.
French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot accused the Iranian authorities at the time of having "detained them without reason for several hours," adding one of them had been "physically manhandled."
Iran said at the time the diplomats had been "briefly questioned" by security services after attending a "meeting with several individuals wanted by the authorities," and denounced French "interference … under the pretext of engaging with civil society."
The Iran-backed Houthis claimed Thursday that they struck three different airports in southwestern Saudi Arabia, and repelled an advance by Saudi-affiliated forces from the southern direction of the Bab el-Mandeb Strait.
Houthi military spokesperson Brig. Gen. Yahya Saree said on X that the group's forces had "succeeded in targeting two military transport aircraft with two ballistic missiles: the first at Najran Airport and the second at King Khalid Air Base in Khamis Mushait," both of which are in southwestern Saudi Arabia.
"Both operations successfully achieved their objectives, by the grace of God," he added.
In a separate statement on X , Saree said Houthi forces earlier thwarted an attempted advance by what he described as Saudi enemy forces "from the southern direction of Bab al-Mandab," the gateway to the Red Sea.
"These force concentrations were targeted with a number of ballistic missiles and heavy weapons, resulting in large numbers of dead and wounded," he said.
In a third statement Tuesday, Saree claimed the Houthis had struck Abha International Airport, also in the Saudi southwest.
"The strike was accurate and led to the disruption of air traffic at the airport," he said.
An oil tanker has caught fire after being caught in the Strait of Hormuz, Iran's navy said on Tuesday.
"Hours ago, a rogue oil tanker that had switched off its tracking systems and was attempting to pass through a prohibited and unsafe area east of the Strait of Hormuz struck naval mines, sustaining damage and catching fire," the navy's public relations office said.
"The Strait of Hormuz is unsafe and closed to rogue ships and vessels attempting to pass through without coordination," it added.
Iran has repeatedly said it will only allow vessels to pass through the waterway if they coordinate with authorities. The U.S. has urged shippers to use a southern route through the strait that Tehran regards as illegal.
Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf said Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei is in "perfect health," describing him as energetic, hopeful and composed following a meeting.

articles.title_orig: Zookeeper dies after she was attacked in leopard enclosure, Dutch safari park says
articles.title_zh: Zookeeper dies after she was attacked in leopard enclosure, Dutch safari park says
articles.content_orig:
An experienced keeper at a Dutch zoo has died days after being mauled in a leopard enclosure, the safari park has confirmed.
The woman, who had worked at Beekse Bergen park for 40 years, was caring for two Persian leopards in an indoor facility when she was attacked on Saturday.
She sustained injuries to her head and neck but despite undergoing surgery, the park confirmed her death on Tuesday.
An independent investigation will be launched into the incident, it added in a statement.
Announcing her death, Beekse Bergen - in the south of the Netherlands - said the keeper began her career there when she was 17 and had worked there on-and-off for four decades.
"Her passing has deeply affected us all, and our hearts go out to her family, friends, and loved ones. At this moment, our primary focus is on supporting her family and her colleagues," the statement added.
The two leopards, which are usually kept away from staff, had been brought inside due to bad weather conditions.
It is not clear exactly what happened in the enclosure because there are no CCTV cameras inside.
Local news website NL Times reported that despite her injures she managed to alert colleagues via her walkie-talkie. She was then taken to hospital in a helicopter in a critical condition before she died days later.
A park spokesperson told Omroep Brabant, a local media outlet, that the leopards were behaving naturally and they would not be euthanised.
"They are, and remain, predators."
Beekse Bergen said it would create a memorial location for guests and staff members to share their condolences.

articles.title_orig: China’s super-secret space plane visible in clearest photo yet
articles.title_zh: China’s super-secret space plane visible in clearest photo yet
articles.content_orig:
The Defense Intelligence Agency (DIA) has released the public’s best look yet at Shenlong, China’s ultra-secret space plane . Details remain scarce on the experimental reusable vehicle , but the unclassified photo offers an unprecedented glimpse of the craft from below, as well as clear views of its unique, rear-facing solar panel arrays.
The photo was taken in 2024 by the geospace intelligence company Maxar Technologies, and is wedged inside the DIA’s latest edition of its Challenges to Security in Space report. The 130-page threat assessment examines the biggest space-based issues currently facing the U.S. and its allies. Although the ever-growing cloud of orbital debris and junk above everyone’s heads remains an international problem, the report also focuses on the near- and long-term aims of countries like China, Russia, Iran, and North Korea.
Located on page 53 of the report, the photo’s caption simply describes it as an unnamed Chinese “spaceplane,” it is almost certainly China’s second reusable orbital vehicle, Shenlong. Very little is known about the project even nearly 20 years after China officially revealed its existence. A Shenlong prototype launched on an initial two-day orbital mission in 2020, followed by a 276-day mission in 2022. Maxar’s 2024 photo coincides with the country’s third known, 268-day orbital test of Shenlong that launched in December 2023. According to the DIA, Shenlong “released and interacted with an object,” but good luck learning much else about it.
The mysterious space plane is reportedly engaged in a fourth excursion after launching from China’s Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center on February 7, 2026. This places it alongside X-37B , the U.S. Space Force’s own secretive robot plane. Designed by Boeing, the reusable vehicle has spent 431 days and counting in low Earth orbit on its eighth classified mission . There is also a bit more available information on the solar-powered spaceplane. The vertical takeoff, horizontal-landing spaceplane measures over 29 feet long, features a nearly 15-foot-long wingspan, and reaches an orbital speed of 17,426 mph. Its full capabilities are unsurprisingly highly classified, although the U.S. Space Force did reveal its eighth mission includes testing cutting-edge laser communications technology as well as quantum measurement instruments.

articles.title_orig: Norway and Finland hold rare call with Putin to discuss ending war
articles.title_zh: Norway and Finland hold rare call with Putin to discuss ending war
articles.content_orig:
The leaders of Finland and Norway have held a joint call with Vladimir Putin - rare contact between the Russian president and European leaders.
Finland's President Alexander Stubb and Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre said the aim of the call had been to "convey messages directly regarding future negotiations" towards peace. An end to the conflict in Ukraine "will not be achieved through silence," Stubb said.
Neither side suggested the needle had been moved on ending the war, which began when Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.
Although the Finnish leader said the conversation with Putin had been "frank and substantive," Støre added that there were "big differences in views" with Putin.
Several European leaders have recently shown willingness to engage with Russia directly, but both Stubb and Støre pointed out their initiative was taken in their capacity as neighbours of Russia, rather than on behalf of Europe as a whole.
"We've not set out to speak on behalf of anyone other than ourselves," Støre said.
Stubb added the call had been prepared in consultation with Ukraine and the US following a meeting between Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, the Nordic leaders and US special envoy Steve Witkoff in Oslo last week.
The first trilateral US-Ukraine-Russia talks since the start of the year are tentatively planned for early November in Abu Dhabi.
Zelensky later confirmed Stubb and Støre debriefed him after the call and said he was grateful for their "active support", while his Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said the call had been "the right approach".
Finland and Norway, which border Russia, initiated the 90-minute call - held from Helsinki - to "discuss Russia's war of aggression against Ukraine and the diplomatic efforts to end the war and promote peace and stability in Europe", the leaders' offices said.
Støre added: "The war comes with enormous human and material costs... The suffering and destruction will impact generations."
The Kremlin said Putin told the leaders that "a just and lasting peace" would only be possible if Russia's interests were considered.
Putin also reaffirmed to the Nordic leaders what he views as the "root causes" of the conflict - his frequent shorthand for Ukraine's desire to exist as a sovereign state.
"A fair long-term peace settlement is possible only if Russia's legal interests are taken into account fully and unconditionally", Putin said.
All three parties reportedly agreed to continue their direct phone communication.
There was no official EU reaction to the talks. The dialogue had not been coordinated with other European leaders, the Danish and Swedish prime ministers said. "I think Europe should stick together rather than going solo," commented Sweden's Ulf Kristersson.
Meanwhile, Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said Stubb had informed him that Europe's position on the upcoming talks in the United Arab Emirates was "moderately optimistic".
Relations between the US and Ukraine and its European allies have soured since US President Donald Trump agreed to lift some sanctions from Russia, allowing Moscow to export oil to the America.
As the Trump administration's position on Russia has softened, several European leaders have said Europe should be trying to re-establish direct contacts with the Kremlin.
Stubb and Støre are the first European leaders to contact Putin since French President Emmanuel Macron's conversation with him in July 2025.
Soon after, Putin visited Alaska for a summit with Trump, and from then on Europeans were further sidelined from Ukraine peace talks. Moscow regularly mocks European leaders and accuses the EU of prolonging the war by supplying Ukraine with weapons.
But last weekend, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said having a European negotiator at the peace talks table would be "good".
And although he said Moscow did not view Finland and Norway as speaking on behalf of Europe, on Tuesday Peskov conceded that Stubb and Støre's talks with Putin had been "very constructive and practical talks with the leaders of two key neighbouring states."

articles.title_orig: Amid the Anthropic IPO excitement, don't forget about earnings season
articles.title_zh: Amid the Anthropic IPO excitement, don't forget about earnings season
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
We are only two days into the week, and it already feels like it should be the weekend.
In the past two days, Meta ( META ) said it will raise $95 billion to support its AI build-out through stock offerings, and Anthropic ( ANTH.PVT ) dropped a 407-page IPO prospectus that I know you haven't read in its entirety. (Wall Street hasn't either, so don't lose sleep over it.)
Lost in that activity is that earnings season continues in full swing, with results from Coca-Cola ( KO ), Hilton ( HLT ), UPS ( UPS ), Whirlpool ( WHR ), and others today.
While investors are jacked up about AI and some stability returning to the tech trade, don't lose sight of earnings season: After all, it's earnings and earnings expectations that power stocks, not Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei (although his comments have moved markets in the past).
So here are a few quick takes on a couple of earnings reports I chewed through this morning:
I don't have any problems with this Hilton quarter, even though the stock is getting hit on a slight revenue miss. The important revenue per available room metric grew 5.8%, the company remains an aggressive buyer of its stock, and it approved the development of 30,500 rooms in the quarter.
The report fits nicely with the Delta ( DAL ) report we got last week, in that higher fuel prices don't appear to be slowing leisure or business travelers.
I think it also fits nicely with the numbers out of UPS today, with US sales up 4.5% and its full-year guidance hike.
Coca-Cola's latest guidance lift reinforces the view that the company continues to take massive market share away from rival PepsiCo ( PEP ). Coke Zero sales surged 16%.
Not a good day for the team at PepsiCo up in Purchase, N.Y.
I continue to be absolutely shocked by what's happening at Whirlpool ( WHR ). Another supersoft quarter, with an adjusted loss of $0.21 per share. Costs are up, and the business is being hurt by a near-frozen US housing market.
You need nerves of steel to buy Whirlpool shares here — the stock is down more than 63% this year. If you do, the thesis has to be that the iconic company is acquired at some point in the next 12 months.

articles.title_orig: The secret succession rankings that Anthropic shareholders will never see (unless the company is ordered)
articles.title_zh: The secret succession rankings that Anthropic shareholders will never see (unless the company is ordered)
articles.content_orig:
Anthropic has devised an unusual way for its founders to pass on their power.
In its IPO filings , Anthropic outlined how seven of its cofounders, who collectively have 50.1% of voting control, will be able to create a ranked list of who they'd like to inherit their power in the event of their death or incapacitation.
What's particularly notable is that while the names would be shared with the other LLC members and Anthropic's Nominating Committee, they are otherwise contractually confidential and generally not public.
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei , Anthropic President Daniela Amodei, and the five other LLC members will review and vote on whether to approve their fellow founders' proposed successors, but the names will likely never be seen by other shareholders. (The agreement allows for the publication only in narrow circumstances, such as a court order or other legal requirement.)
Under the agreement, which was first highlighted by Forbes , each member of the Founders LLC may name up to 10 potential successors, ranked in order of preference. The other LLC members must then vote to approve the secret lists.
While succession plans are not unusual, Anthropic's approach is unusual in how it ranks potential successors. It also underscores how, thanks to the Founders LLC, Anthropic's leaders will be able to maintain control as shareholders begin to offer input post-IPO.
Facebook's 2012 IPO paperwork suggested that if Mark Zuckerberg were in control of the company at the time of his death, then control could be transferred to someone he designated. (Meta has since tweaked this plan.) In 2020, Airbnb's three cofounders agreed to transfer their voting power to their other cofounders if one of them died or became disabled, but that arrangement (which still exists) only lasts for nine months.
The succession plan does not establish CEO succession. Anthropic's board of directors would handle such a chief executive appointment.
There are also some limitations to who the Anthropic founders can name on their lists.
Add BI in Google so our reporting is easier to find when you’re searching for what matters.
Eight of their 10 potential successors are subject to eligibility requirements, including that the person named is a current or former employee of Anthropic or one of its subsidiaries, or has worked for "a 501(c)(3) tax-exempt organization or a national or international organization whose primary purpose is research, education, or the promotion of public benefit." In either case, the person must have worked there for at least three years.
If the person worked for Anthropic, they must have held a specific role, such as a member of the technical staff or the company's internal think tank, or another role approved by the board and a majority of the other members. If they worked outside Anthropic, they must have held a senior role at the nonprofit. These successors must also be US citizens, have permanent residency, or have valid work authorization.
The other two names, if a founder names all 10 potential successors, are not subject to the eligibility requirements, but they must also receive the required approval.
The succession plan doesn't last forever.
Under the agreement, a successor member generally would cease to be a member on the 10th anniversary of Anthropic's IPO. After that point, successor designees may be admitted only in limited circumstances during a transition period.

articles.title_orig: Fed meeting live updates: Federal Reserve weighs elevated inflation, midterm elections as October meeting kicks off
articles.title_zh: Fed meeting live updates: Federal Reserve weighs elevated inflation, midterm elections as October meeting kicks off
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
The Federal Reserve kicked off its two-day policy meeting on Tuesday as elevated inflation continues to pose a problem for central bankers who nevertheless seem reluctant to hike rates this month.
Fed watchers expect the central bank to keep benchmark rates in the 3.75% to 4% range , with bond traders pricing in a less than 10% chance of a hike on Wednesday, per CME Group. A rate hike in December appears far more likely, however, according to the Fed's dot plot and fed funds futures.
Although recent inflation data came in hotter than expected , several officials' remarks suggest the Fed will hold rates this month to continue assessing additional data. The proximity of the October meeting to the US midterm elections next Tuesday is also seen as a deterrent to bold monetary policy moves.
With the Fed holding rates steady seen as all but given, the focus is on what Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh will say at his post-FOMC-meeting press conference on Wednesday. Warsh has deliberately avoided telegraphing future Fed policy moves, but hot inflation could elicit more insight from him into the path forward.
The Federal Open Market Committee's two-day policy meeting has started and will conclude at 2 p.m. ET on Wednesday.
The FOMC's decision on whether to cut, hold, or raise interest rates will be released at 2 p.m. tomorrow. Following that decision, Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh will hold a news conference at 2:30 p.m. that will be live-streamed.
This is the seventh FOMC meeting this year. The final Fed meeting of the year will take place from Dec. 8-9 and will include a Summary of Economic Projections, which will be used to gauge where policymakers see rates heading in 2027.
The Federal Reserve heads into its interest-rate decision this week facing hotter inflation, keeping the meeting live even as markets widely expect the central bank to hold interest rates steady just days before the midterm elections.
Alan Blinder, a former Fed vice chair and a Princeton University economics professor, is expecting a "hawkish pause."
Although Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh doesn't favor telegraphing the central bank's next move, Blinder said the moment calls for clarity.
"This is a perfect time for clear forward guidance that doesn't quite say, but strongly hints, we're pausing now, but we stand ready to raise again and even give a hint that the next meeting might be the next interest rate hike."
The Federal Reserve's two-day policy meeting kicked off this morning at 9:30 a.m. ET, as scheduled, a Fed spokesperson confirmed.
Expectations remain firm that the Fed will hold rates steady in a range of 3.75% to 4% after hiking by 25 basis points in September. Traders broadly view that the Fed will hike again in December.
But in October, there's a strong belief the Fed won't move rates. According to CME Group's FedWatch, traders see a 90% chance of no move.

articles.title_orig: Federal Reserve expected to hold interest rates steady in last decision before midterm elections
articles.title_zh: Federal Reserve expected to hold interest rates steady in last decision before midterm elections
articles.content_orig:
Navy Federal Credit Union chief economist Heather Long discusses the Federal Reserve's upcoming interest rate decisions.
The Federal Reserve is set to announce its latest interest rate decision on Wednesday with the midterm elections less than a week away.
Policymakers at the Fed say they avoid letting politics influence their monetary policy moves, and can be hesitant to hike or cut interest rates at meetings that occur ahead of the election.
Inflation has remained stubbornly high and the September consumer price index (CPI) data showed inflation rose faster than expected, with headline CPI rising 0.6% on a monthly basis and 3.7% from a year ago. The latter figure is well above the central bank's 2% inflation target.
Heather Long, chief economist at Navy Federal Credit Union, told FOX Business in an interview that while the September inflation data was hotter than expected and raised the prospects of an October rate hike, the Fed is likely to wait to "hike again in December."
CONSUMER INFLATION ROSE FASTER THAN EXPECTED IN SEPTEMBER, CPI REPORT SHOWS
Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh and policymakers are expected to hold rates steady this week. (Daniel Heuer/Bloomberg via Getty Images)
"This hotter than expected inflation data did increase the chance of an October rate hike , but it's a very high bar to increase in October, they would do it within a week of the election. I know they like to say that they're not political, but it's a high bar for October," she explained.
"Right now, this data indicates that the Fed needs to act again, but it's not a five-alarm fire. They don't have to act immediately, they could wait until December."
"The reality is, gas prices have come down a little bit since the September highs, so we would expect the October data – you know, it won't be great, but it could be a little bit cooler than what we're seeing today. And the Fed has a reasonable case to say, we're probably still gonna hike, but let's wait a few more weeks and see just how broad-based this problem really is," Long said.
FEDERAL RESERVE HIKES INTEREST RATES FOR FIRST TIME SINCE 2023 AMID STUBBORN INFLATION
The market expects the Fed to hold rates steady this week, with the CME FedWatch tool showing a 90.6% probability of rates remaining at their current target range of 3.75% to 4% – up from 84.5% a week ago and 35.8% last month.
For the Fed's meeting in mid-December, the tool shows a 75.1% probability of a 25-basis-point interest rate hike, which could mark the resumption of the rate-hiking cycle if inflation remains elevated.
WHY THE FED ISN'T READY TO DECLARE VICTORY ON INFLATION
Inflation rose faster than expected in September and remains well above the central bank's 2% target. (Robert Nickelsberg/Getty Images)
"The Federal Reserve will definitely hike interest rates again, probably in December," Long said. "The big question is how many more times do they have to hike after that? And what was scary in this latest inflation data for September is to see so many areas of hot inflation: to see used car prices, airfares, recreation costs, auto repair costs, buying a used car, medical costs."
"The story really is starting to take shape that it's probably going to take a couple more hikes in 2027, and this higher-for-longer borrowing costs and mortgage rates well above 7% is going to stick around for at least a year, maybe longer," Long said.

articles.title_orig: US consumer confidence recovers in October as gas prices eased a bit
articles.title_zh: US consumer confidence recovers in October as gas prices eased a bit
articles.content_orig:
Kitco NEWS has a diverse team of journalists reporting on the economy, stock markets, commodities, cryptocurrencies, mining and metals with accuracy and objectivity. Our goal is to help people make informed market decisions through in-depth reporting, daily market roundups, interviews with prominent industry figures, comprehensive coverage (often exclusive) of important industry events and analyses of market-affecting developments.
(Kitco News) - Gold prices are trading at session highs after the latest data showed an improving picture of the attitudes of U.S. consumers this month.
The Consumer Confidence Index rose to 91.7 in October, above economists’ consensus forecast for an 81 reading and also above the upwardly revised 84.2 print from September, the Conference Board announced on Tuesday.
The Present Situation Index—based on consumers' assessment of current business and labor market conditions—increased by 8.6 points to 120.4. The Expectations Index—based on consumers' short-term outlook for income, business, and labor market conditions—recovered by 6.9 points to 72.6, only partially reversing three consecutive monthly declines. The survey period for this month's preliminary results was October 1 - 21.
Gold prices were setting fresh session highs in the wake of the 10 am ET data release, with spot gold last trading at $4,048.48 per ounce at the time of writing for a gain of 0.78% on the daily chart.
“Consumer confidence advanced in October, driven primarily by improved perceptions of current and expected business conditions,” said Fergus McCormick, Senior Economist, Global Indicators at The Conference Board. “The recovery was in line with retail gasoline prices easing from September to October. Yet, despite the increase in October, consumer confidence remained on the long-term downward trend that's persisted over the past few years. Consumers planned less spending on services and durable goods over the next six months. This likely reflected higher price levels and persistent inflation, which eroded consumers' purchasing power.”
“Among write-in responses in October, consumers continued to express frustration with rising costs,” he added. “References to prices, the high cost of food and groceries, and oil and diesel prices rose. Comments about war and conflict eased for a second straight month but remained elevated. Mentions of jobs and employment as an area of concern also ticked up, though to a lesser extent.”
“On a six-month moving average basis, only consumers under age 35 and those with a household income of $100k or more expressed an increase in confidence,” the report noted. “By generation, confidence amongst Gen X, Baby Boomers, and the Silent Generation continued to trail significantly behind Gen Z and Millennials, widening a sharp generational divide that has emerged over the past two years. In October, confidence improved across all political affiliations—but much more so for Republicans.”
Consumers' average 12-month inflation expectations declined in October but remained elevated at 5.8%,” the Conference Board said. “Consumers still expected higher interest rates over the next 12 months. Overall, more consumers in October expected stock prices to increase rather than decrease in the next 12 months.”
Jeffrey Roach, Chief Economist at LPL Financial, noted that business conditions and discretionary spending both improved in October.
"Business conditions are the best since April when consensus believed the war with Iran would be short-lived, inflation was less sticky, and the AI-trade dominated headlines," he said. "Even more noteworthy, the top five spending plans included restaurants and movies. Several discretionary sectors are vibrant, although consumers said they will cut back on hotels and airfare."
Roach pointed out that employment opportunities also appeared more plentiful, and home buying plans improved for the third consecutive month.
"Consumers may be tightening their belts, but some experiences are still a priority," he said. "Given the other data on core capital shipments, auto sales, and broader consumer spending, Q3 economic growth will likely be above 3% as the economy plows ahead, elevating annual growth to 2.2% for the full year."

articles.title_orig: US Army looks to high-flying balloons to help see, strike along front lines with China
articles.title_zh: US Army looks to high-flying balloons to help see, strike along front lines with China
articles.content_orig:
To burst China’s anti-access/area-denial bubble, the U.S. Army is looking at using high-flying balloons with payloads that can monitor the battlefield, relay communications and strike adversaries.
The Army has tinkered with high-altitude balloons for some time, but interest and experimentation have grown in recent years. Against China’s growing arsenal in the vastness of the Pacific , those balloons could provide a cheaper, lower-signature platform that can be employed from dispersed positions, Maj. Gen. Bernard Harrington, commander of the Army’s 7th Infantry Division/Multi-Domain Command-Pacific, or MDC-P, said at the Association of the U.S. Army’s annual conference in Washington, D.C., earlier this month.
Harrington’s command was recently established to merge the ground-maneuver elements of the 7th Infantry Division and long-range capabilities of the 1st Multi-Domain Task Force. Part of the unit’s mission is to operate in space, cyberspace and the electromagnetic spectrum and use long-range fires to help the rest of the Joint Force maneuver, including by opening gaps in China’s anti-access/area-denial network — the air, sea and land-based sensors and weapons designed to keep U.S. forces at bay.
“For us in the Pacific, we really are looking at a specific pacing threat and an anti-access/area-denial network,” against which MDC-P aims to create “windows of opportunity for that Joint Force, whether it be a carrier strike group that’s going to pulse into the weapons engagement zone , whether it be a bomber task force, whether it be a ground unit doing a joint forcible-entry operation,” Harrington said.
High-altitude balloons, or HABs, could facilitate that by carrying “launched effects” — the Army’s term for an aerial system deployed from crewed and uncrewed vehicles for reconnaissance, communications, strikes and other missions. HABs would give MDC-P soldiers more ways to employ attack drones and munitions that are cheaper than “exquisite” missiles, available in greater numbers and harder for adversaries to spot.
Interest in HABs has grown in part due to technological improvements that allow them to stay aloft for weeks or months at a time and give operators more control over where they go. That enhances balloons’ value as platforms for radars and other sensors which, at operating altitudes above 60,000 feet, can see far into rival territory while remaining in international airspace. They also offer a cost-effective complement to satellites, which are more expensive and whose orbits limit their time over any one area.
Harrington described high-altitude balloons as part of “an ecosystem” of data-collecting assets in space, in the air, on land and at sea. HABs in particular could compensate if space-based assets are taken out , Harrington said. “So our ability to employ HABs [and] have HABs be persistent enables both our collection and targeting as well as us [to] provide that information to the Joint Force for their collection and targeting.”
Harrington also described a role for balloon- or unmanned surface vessel-launched effects in kinetic strikes. With the right timing and enough precision, those strikes may not even need to eliminate their target to create an opening.
“Maybe I don’t necessarily need to sink a ship, but if I take out certain systems on that vessel, well, then it creates this temporal window of opportunity,” Harrington said.
“We saw great value [in] that maybe I don’t have to use specifically or unmask an exquisite system to achieve that effect. If I can achieve effect of mass utilizing lower-cost systems, maybe that will get me there,” Harrington added. “So we modeled that, and what we saw was — particularly with our unmanned surface vessels, long-range one-way attack, long-range launched effects — the ability to synchronize and mass that could potentially get us to achieve that effect.”
Harrington’s command experimented with some of those systems during Bayonet Quest 26, an exercise held in Michigan and on Lake Huron from late September to early October. An official video showed soldiers working with air and maritime drones, including a quadcopter launched from a surface vessel and a fixed-wing drone hooked up to a balloon. Harrington said Bayonet Quest tested MDC-P’s ability to “orchestrate those systems” by launching them, gathering data from their sensors, and using AI and LLMs to process that data and produce tasking orders.
“If you see [a potential target], then task a UAS to be able to come over and actually validate if that meets the target folder,” Harrington said, describing the approach. “Then I can task long-range one-way attack [or] an attack USV to be able to achieve that effect or I could send that as a potential fire mission to a more exquisite munition to be able to close that kill chain.”
That reduces the need for a large, easily targetable ground presence, Harrington added: “This is all about integration: Integrate multiple systems into one data layer, be able to lay something like a large language model on top of it, and allow orchestration so we don’t have a lot of soldiers in fixed sites on ground control stations.”
Harrington’s comments come amid a flurry of HAB-related experiments by the Army in North Africa , the Middle East , Europe and the Pacific.
At exercise Valiant Shield in Guam this summer, soldiers experimented with HABs and launched effects “within an island-chain operational construct.” One test sent a HAB aloft towing a long-endurance drone “to evaluate stratospheric payload deployment capabilities.” Soldiers tested the same balloon-drone combo in Japan during Orient Shield in September.
The Army’s Multi-Domain Command-Europe has done dozens of HAB launches over the past year to examine the logistics of employing balloons and to test sensing and communications capabilities using “ experimental payloads .”
Speaking alongside Harrington this month, MDC-E commander Brig. Gen. Steven Carpenter said HABs have a role, alongside other sensors and weapons, in opening “windows of opportunity” against anti-access/area-denial networks, in particular by providing resilient communications and additional strike platforms.
“We like to proliferate the stratosphere with high-altitude balloons, but I mean 200, 300 at a time. We like to use them as drones, [communications retransmission], electromagnetic sensing, electronic attack, and then to drop them down and have air-launched effects,” Carpenter said. “During different seasons, the flight paths are different. We study that. We understand during what seasons, where the best places are to launch those high-altitude systems and then, again, to hold enemy cities and capabilities at risk at any time.”

articles.title_orig: Anduril and Qualcomm Plan to Build Laptop With US Supply Chain
articles.title_zh: Anduril and Qualcomm Plan to Build Laptop With US Supply Chain
articles.content_orig:
BlueChip is a new line of laptops coming in 2027 from Anduril and Qualcomm, starting with a rugged military-focused model.﻿
BlueChip is a new line of laptops coming in 2027 from Anduril and Qualcomm, starting with a rugged military-focused model.﻿
Anduril and Qualcomm are partnering on a new line of laptops called BlueChip, launching in early 2027. The first prototype is a ruggedized model using Arm-based Snapdragon X series chips and aimed at the US military, but the ultimate focus of the joint venture is to make laptops entirely in the US. Eventually.
The global supply chain of computers and laptops normally involves China, Taiwan, and many other countries, so the first BlueChip laptops will only be “designed and assembled in the United States,” per Anduril’s official press release. Assembly is planned to be done at Anduril’s Arsenal-1 facility in Ohio.
Anduril and Qualcomm aren’t sharing many details on how they’re going to build enough manufacturing in the US for a laptop that’s 100-percent domestically made. During a virtual Q&A session with media that included The Verge , Anduril founder Palmer Luckey and Qualcomm CEO Cristiano Amon laid out the motivations for American-made (or at least, American-assembled) laptops. It’s the talking points you’d expect: keeping US money in the US, the potential for creating domestic jobs, minimizing technological / economic reliance on other countries, and reducing national security vulnerabilities.
When asked what percentage of the BlueChip laptop’s components will be made in the US once it launches in 2027, Luckey said, “TBD. . . Those questions are not settled.” The components Luckey specified that are planned to be American-made from the start are the display glass, the frame around the display, and parts of the ribbon component. “I think most likely the thing that we ship is not going to be 100-percent American.” It sounds like BlueChip’s first laptop will be well below the 65-percent requirement to count as American-made under federal procurement rules. A promo image provided by Anduril shows hardware stamped with “Built in America.”
As for the chips in BlueChip, Qualcomm’s Amon told The Verge it intends to manufacture processors for this laptop at TSMC Arizona. When The Verge followed up to ask how much money Qualcomm is investing into that, Qualcomm communications rep Yelena Tebcherani said, “We don’t have any more details to share at the moment.”
Anduril’s first potential customer for BlueChip laptops is the same as its drones: the US military. The prototype is a ruggedized computer aimed at military personnel, complete with a rifle strap-style carrying handle — presumably so a soldier can slam the laptop shut, quickly grab it, and get on the move. It will run Windows or two undisclosed versions of Linux.
During the Q&A, Luckey indicated that BlueChip is funded entirely by Anduril and Qualcomm, not government subsidies. He mentioned that Anduril is starting with a military laptop to first service users with the most stringent hardware needs and software security demands. It’s also likely for pursuing those valuable government contracts that could call for large quantities of expensive computers. After the government and defense sectors, Anduril’s next target will be first responders and public safety, before eventually getting to consumer-level laptops — the lowest on the priority list. Luckey mentioned offhandedly, “I’d say the worst case here is that this is going to be a low volume laptop for critical industries and government needs that desperately need something like this to exist.”
Palmer Luckey is of course a controversial figure, with his history of fueling right wing troll farms motivated by his political beliefs . Anduril is better known for making drones and autonomous weapons , while Luckey continues making consumer-facing products like Game Boy clones — often polarizing the communities they’re meant to serve. Bringing a supply chain for computers back to the US and one day manufacturing a fully American-made laptop sounds a tall order. It’s complicated even further once you consider the person and company behind it.
Correction, October 27th: Palmer Luckey is Anduril’s founder, not CEO, as this story initially stated.

AT&T Inc. customers affected by two cybersecurity breaches in 2024 could start receiving payments soon, after a federal judge granted final approval to a $177 million class action settlement earlier this month.
AT&T ( T ) agreed to a settlement resolving a lawsuit alleging the company failed to implement adequate cybersecurity measures to protect customers' personal information following the 2024 data breaches.
On March 30, 2024, the company said that a data set released on the dark web contained AT&T customer information. On July 12, 2024, AT&T announced a second data breach in which limited data was illegally downloaded from an AT&T workspace on a third-party cloud platform.
The company denies any wrongdoing. The U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Texas approved the deal on Oct. 2. If an appeal is not filed, the settlement's date is estimated to be on Nov. 12.
Read more: Just received a settlement? Here are 5 smart ways to use the money.
The deadline to submit a claim has passed, but customers were eligible to submit a claim and receive a payment if their personal information was compromised in one or both of the data breach incidents.
The deadline to submit a claim was Dec. 18, 2025, but customers who did submit a claim on time can visit TelecomDataSettlement.com for the most recent information.

Members who fall into the first settlement class and have a documented loss that occurred in 2019 or later are eligible for a cash payment of up to $5,000.
Those who fall into the second settlement class for losses that occurred on or after April 14, 2024, may receive a payment of up to $2,500.
As an alternative to a documented loss cash payment, eligible class members also had the option to submit a claim for a pro rata share of the remaining settlement fund after payment of settlement administration costs, attorneys' fees, costs, and service awards.
Payments must be distributed electronically or by paper check within 60 days of the effective date, or the official date when the terms of the settlement can no longer be appealed.

articles.title_orig: Frontier AI labs say their models refuted the Exponential Time Hypothesis. What does that mean?
articles.title_zh: Frontier AI labs say their models refuted the Exponential Time Hypothesis. What does that mean?
articles.content_orig:

OpenAI released solutions to three blockbuster math problems that have long vexed researchers. One was a surprise rejection of the Exponential Time Hypothesis (ETH), a durable assumption in computer science that plays a large role in how we understand what is difficult to compute.
As with previous proof-drops from the frontier lab, scientific communities responded with a mixture of thrill and dismay. Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge suggested that OpenAI was basing its solutions on pre-existing work, and hours later, Anthropic subsequently released its own refutation of ETH.
However, OpenAI’s process is evolving. This time, the lab structured its releases differently for each of the three disciplines involved: Mathematicians got the work dropped on GitHub; the computer scientists formed a working group, asked for the proofs to be shared publicly and OpenAI to fund a conference to discuss them; the physicists formed a working group that will determine how their result will be released.
MIT professor Ryan Williams is the computer scientist who is organizing his field’s response to the new finding. Williams, whose work focuses on these questions of computational complexity, has criticized OpenAI’s approach in the past, calling its proof dump earlier this October a “DDOS attack on mathematicians.”
However, he agreed to collaborate with the frontier labs in order to help shepherd ideas that are vital to the field, he told TechCrunch. The lab asked him to help interpret the solution, along with UC San Diego computer scientists Russell Impagliazzo and Ramamohan Paturi, who first published the ETH in 1999.
Their first step was to release an open letter calling for feedback from scientists interested in these problems and a discussion of the norms around AI contributions to their work.
“Some parts [of OpenAI’s proof] are, maybe you could say routine, but then yes, there are two or three alien-looking parts, and it’s exactly these parts that I saw that made me think, wow, this is something that the whole community needs to work on together,” Williams told TechCrunch.
The ETH is part of a broader class of problems known as P versus NP, which has animated computer science and many other fields for decades. Reductively, researchers are trying to understand if any problem whose solution can be easily verified (NP) can also be easily solved (P).
A simple example is the game Sodoku: Once a solution to a puzzle is in place, it can be quickly verified, but finding the solution is time-consuming. That dynamic is true across a range of important problems, and the insight underpins cryptographic systems: When you have the key to an encoded message, you can reveal it, but actually cracking an effective code takes too long to be useful.
However, scientists have yet to prove whether that is always true. “P = NP is saying that, not only can you verify Sudoku solutions when they exist, you can just generate them,” Williams said. “P = NP is asserting that this is true for every single problem you can verify quickly — if you can verify it quickly, you can solve it quickly. So this just seems too good to be true.”
That’s why most scientists assume that P ≠ NP. ETH provided evidence for that. It basically says that even the fastest computer algorithm needs exponentially more time to find a solution as the number of variables grow in a specific class of tricky logic puzzle.
The claims from OpenAI and Anthropic is that their models have come up with algorithms that solve those puzzles in “sub-exponential” time, meaning faster than the speeds previously thought possible. If true, they may have proven the EFT to be false — refuted it, in scientific terms — and maybe opened up a path for algorithms that generally perform P = NP.
“Every computer scientist should probably put a little more weight on the plausibility of P = NP, but one’s weight may vary,” Williams said. “I do think that it kind of calls into question a lot of the intuitions that we thought we had about … how tractable [hard NP problems] are. I also think that this is probably not the final answer either. I don’t think that OpenAI’s algorithm could possibly be the best algorithm you can get.”
The durability of ETH has lead to it being included in many scientific papers over the past decade that will need to be revisited if the AI labs claims that they’ve proven it wrong holds up, Williams said.
“This is partly why I was asking or pushing OpenAI to support a conference on this — it’s going to affect many researchers’ works, and we need to figure out, okay, what happens next besides understanding the algorithms. We need to understand, how should the foundations change compared to what we had before?” he said. Before scientific concerns, there are cybersecurity questions. Williams said that an improved algorithm could imply that cryptographic systems relying on certain key sizes could be considered broken. So one of the first questions he asked OpenAI science lead Dan Roberts “was if they had checked that this affects any crypto systems … is anything insecure now? And apparently, they checked, and they were reasonably confident that this didn’t … imply any breaks.”
This new AI paradigm of scientific discovery is still a work in progress, but Williams says he is optimistic despite real concerns, particularly about training the next generation of scientists. Being a computer scientist who does high level math has perhaps made the adjustment easier for him than for pure mathematicians.
Still, he says AI is “forcing people to be a little more ambitious about the kind of work that they do, and to think more deeply about, okay, if all the things I used to work on are now low-hanging fruit for AI, how can I raise the bar for the kind of scientific questions I want to ask?”

The Dallas-based investment firm Disruptive, whose past bets include Palantir, Airbnb, and Spotify, announced a $10 billion fund to back at least 10 late-stage companies, with checks of up to $1 billion, it said Tuesday .
It’s one of the biggest fundraises of the year so far, aiming to back (what else?!) the capital-intensive fields of AI and defense. The Wall Street Journal first reported earlier this month that the firm was seeking to raise the fund and by then had already secured at least $7.5 billion in capital commitments.
The firm was founded in 2012 by Alex Davis, grandson of billionaire oil magnate Marvin Davis.
This is technically the firm’s first blind-pool fund, meaning investors commit money without knowing which companies it will back. Until now, the firm raised money through deal-by-deal special purpose vehicles . Disruptive has nonetheless made headlines in recent years for pouring money into companies like chip startup Groq and the AI voice-generation startup ElevenLabs. Bloomberg reported that the firm told LPs it has returned more than $6 billion on the roughly $1.9 billion it has put into startups.
According to the Dallas Business Journal, the new vehicle is the largest venture fund raised in Texas history.

Maxime took home the coveted sword at SPIEL in Germany last weekend for this amazing take on the legendary Ultramarines warrior, Marneus Calgar .

articles.title_orig: Who Is Zhang Yiming? China's Richest Person Again
articles.title_zh: Who Is Zhang Yiming? China's Richest Person Again
articles.content_orig:
Beijing — ByteDance founder Zhang Yiming reclaimed the top spot on a list of China's richest people, driven by his company's push into artificial intelligence.
The rankings released by The Hurun Research Institute on Tuesday reflected that the country's high-tech sectors were rising while others, like the consumer sector and real estate, were under pressure.
The institute, which has published the list annually since 1999, found a record 1,529 people with more than 5 billion yuan (about $750 million), up 6.6% from last year.
The number of billionaires based on their net worth in U.S. dollars rose to 1,176, up 155 people - 176 more than in the U.S. That was slightly below the 1,185 people in 2021.
Zhang topped the list with $100 billion, up 43%, "almost all of it on the back of AI," and the amount was a record high for China's richest person, Rupert Hoogewerf, Hurun Report chairman, said in a statement. Hoogewerf noted that ByteDance's Doubao is China's most used AI assistant.
AI is the biggest single wealth engine on the list: 160 people - one in 10 - now make their money from AI, he said.
ByteDance is the parent company of popular short-video platforms TikTok and Douyin.
TikTok's U.S.-based operations were shifted to a new joint venture in January made up mostly of American investors due to years of national security-related concerns that almost got TikTok banned in the U.S. ByteDance still holds a minority stake in TikTok's U.S. arm.
One of the investors in TikTok's U.S. venture is Oracle, a tech company chaired by Larry Ellison. His son David Ellison is co-CEO of Skydance Corp., the parent company of CBS News.
Bottled water magnate Zhong Shanshan fell to second place on the list with $61 billion, down 23%, while Robin Zeng, chairman of CATL, the world's largest maker of batteries for electric vehicles, came in third, Hurun said.
Hurun cross-checked its information with entrepreneurs, regulators, industry experts and others to compile the list, while acknowledging limitations.
Chinese artificial intelligence startup DeepSeek founder Liang Wenfeng, a new face on the list, ranked seventh. AI chipmaker Cambricon chair Chen Tianshi was 10th.
"This year's gains were polarised - entrepreneurs in AI, semiconductors and robotics surged ahead, whilst those in consumer, real estate and traditional manufacturing saw their wealth shrink - a two-speed economy," Hoogewerf said.
China last week said its economy grew 4.5% in the July-September quarter from a year ago, fueled by robust exports, moving closer to meeting its official annual growth target for 2026. For the entire year, Chinese leaders have set a growth target of 4.5% to 5%, down from last year's 5% expansion.
While some industries were thriving thanks to government support for technologies such as AI and electric vehicles, owners of small businesses reported tough times as their customers cut back on spending.
China's domestic demand has been weighed down by a yearslong downturn in its property market.
The Hurun list reflected that, as well.
Hoogewerf said Lei Jun, chairman of Chinese smart consumer electronics maker Xiaomi, was this year's "biggest faller," with his wealth halved to $25.1 billion. Consumer fortunes also fell across the board, Hoogewerf said.
"Today, for the first time ever, not a single mainland property developer remains in the Top 100 - the only property names left at the top are the Hong Kong landlord families," he said.
